args: Analyze the root cause and safest minimal fix for unsafe string comparisons in `dissect_softether_host_fqdn` in `src/lib/protocols/softether.c`. In particular, determine the semantics and trustworthiness of `val1.value_size`, `val1.value.ptr.value_str`, `val2.value_size`, and any local serialized `value_siz`, and identify whether nearby tuple parsers have related length/accounting risks that must be fixed to address this crash at its root.

The supplied ASan report shows a one-byte use-after-poison in `strncmp`, called at `src/lib/protocols/softether.c:236` from `dissect_softether_host_fqdn`, reached through UDP SoftEther detection. The vulnerability statement says attacker-controlled `val2.value_size` is used as the extent in `strncmp(val2.value.ptr.value_str, "ddns_fqdn", val2.value_size)`, and similarly a serialized `value_siz` is used for `host_name`. The requested remediation is exact expected-literal length checks, then comparisons bounded to `NDPI_STATICSTRING_LEN(...)`, using `val1.value_size` for `host_name`. No edits have yet been made; I am inspecting parsing semantics before applying the minimal C-source fix.
